articles.title: Broadway Box Office: 'Hamilton' Rises Back Up to $3M, 'Here There are Blueberries' Cracks $1M
articles.summary: 'Inter Alia,' starring Rosamund Pike, is also continuing to build momentum.
articles.content:
Hamilton was the top grossing show last week, rising back above $3 million as the industry neared its lucrative holiday week, followed by Other Desert Cities with $2.5 million and the Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell-led Much Ado About Nothing , which still brought in $2 million in a week that included its comped opening night performance.

The Lion King followed with $1.9 million and Harry Potter and the Cursed Child with $1.7 million.

Inter Alia, starring Rosamund Pike, continues to build momentum, bringing in close to $1 million ($993,103) with 100 percent capacity, across its first week of seven performances. The play is set to open Dec. 1.

Here There are Blueberries , a play about museum curators examining previously undiscovered photos from the Holocaust, cracked $1 million for the first time since beginning previews in early November. The show played to close to 100 percent capacity with an average ticket price of $128.

New musical Galileo saw a slight dip in capacity and grosses after lead actor Raúl Esparza missed performances from Nov. 16 through Nov. 18 while recovering from a concussion. The show brought in $699,975 across six performances, and saw capacity fall to 92 percent. The musical is scheduled to open Dec. 6.

Wanted, a new musical which opened Nov. 8, also saw a dip in capacity down to 85 percent, with the show grossing $661,143 across eight performances.

Broadway’s holiday fare has not yet taken off with consumers, with The Blue Man Group playing to 60 percent capacity, illusionist show Now You See Me playing to 77 percent capacity and radio play It’s a Wonderful Life playing to 76 percent.

articles.title: TV Ratings: NBA Logs Winning Streak in First Month of the Season
articles.summary: Audiences on national media partners NBC/Peacock, ESPN and Prime Video are up by 37 percent year to year.
articles.content:
Like a jump shooter who can't miss, the NBA is on a heater with TV audiences through the first month of its 2026-27 season.

National telecasts of league games on NBC/Peacock, ESPN and Prime Video are averaging 2.62 million viewers over the season's first month, based on Nielsen ratings and Adobe Analytics figures for Peacock's games. That's a sizable, 37 percent increase over the same time frame last year — the first in the league's current media rights deal with NBCUniversal, ESPN and Prime Video. Through last week, every national telecast had topped 1 million viewers, the first time that's happened since 2023. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV TV Ratings: CMA Awards Score Seven-Year High TV Streaming Ratings: Rough Week for Original Series, 'From' Remains No. 1 Overall

That's also the highest mark on record for the first month of an NBA season, excluding lockout-delayed starts in 1999 and 2011 (and with the caveat that changes in Nielsen measurement the past few years have tended to benefit live sports).

NBC's six national windows lead the way with an average of 4.5 million viewers (including streaming on Peacock), a 27 percent improvement over last season's first month.. The network's opening night game between the defending champion New York Knicks and the Philadelphia 76ers (who acquired LeBron James during the offseason) averaged 7.71 million cross-platform viewers.

The first eight games on Prime Video have averaged 2.05 million viewers, and ESPN is at 1.8 million viewers across 13 telecasts. Prime Video has grown by a huge 83 percent year to year, and ESPN's games are up 13 percent.

Prime Video has the youngest audience of the NBA's three national media partners (the same is true for Prime relative to other NFL broadcasters); its median viewer age is a little under 46. ESPN and NBC (not including Peacock viewers) have a median age of about 53 for NBA games.

articles.title: Stephen King Was Outed as Richard Bachman Thanks to This Book That Was Turned Into a Movie 30 Years Ago
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Paramount Pictures It has been 30 years since a movie came out based on the Stephen King novel that outed the author as Richard Bachman. When King was breaking into the novel industry, he found himself pigeonholed into the horror genre. With instant hits like Carrie, 'Salem's Lot, and The Shining, King was expected to keep writing […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It has been 30 years since a movie came out based on the Stephen King novel that outed the author as Richard Bachman. When King was breaking into the novel industry, he found himself pigeonholed into the horror genre. With instant hits like Carrie , ' Salem's Lot , and The Shining , King was expected to keep writing horror, but he wanted to try to write in other genres too. While he has mostly stuck with horror over his career, King is much more than that. As Richard Bachman, he released sci-fi ( The Running Man ), thrillers ( The Long Walk ), and even intense psychological dramas ( Roadwork ).

In 1984, King wrote a horror novel under the Richard Bachman pseudonym , and it quickly led to fans connecting the dots and realizing that King was Bachman. After he retired the Bachman pseudonym, the novel ended up being adapted into a movie. Thinner came out in theaters on October 25, 1996, and it gave movie fans a look at the story that King wrote behind his assumed identity.

Thinner Helped Reveal Stephen King's Pseudonym Image Courtesy of Paramount Pictures Most of King's novels under the name Richard Bachman were not horror stories, although they all had terrifying premises. Rage was a book about a high school student who killed two of his teachers and took his classmates hostage. The Running Man was about a deadly reality TV show , written years before reality TV was even a thing in real life. Roadwork was about a man barricading himself in his house to prevent the state from demolishing it to build a freeway. These are not the stories one might expect from the King of Horror. However, Thinner was exactly what people would expect from Stephen King.

Thinner follows an obese upper-class attorney named Billy Halleck who has a wife and daughter. He is not an ethical attorney and recently defended a mafia boss and got him acquitted of a murder charge. After celebrating the victory, he is involved in an accident while driving where he runs over an elderly Romani woman, killing her. He is acquitted of manslaughter in a case presided over by his friend, a judge, and thanks in part to the police chief committing perjury in the trial. However, he doesn't get away with it because the woman's father, Tadzu Lempke, places a curse on Billy on the steps of the courthouse.

What happens next is that Billy starts to lose weight rapidly despite not exercising or eating right. Billy soon learns that the judge and police chief were also cursed, with one becoming a lizard-like being and the other getting ulcers on his face and hands. They both die by suicide, but Billy fights to find a way to survive the curse, even as he begins to waste away. It was pure horror, with the morality tale carrying it to the end. The ending even has the double twist that King is best known for, where the seeming victory comes with a bitter defeat, and Billy realizes he will never escape the curse, one way or the other.

While King created an entire fictional biography for Richard Bachman, and even used a photo of one of his literary agent's friends, fans began to suspect the truth. Some began to send angry letters, accusing Bachman of copying King's style, while others began to wonder if Bachman was a pseudonym. This led to a bookstore employee in Washington, D.C., who was a huge King fan, discovering the truth. This man looked at the copyright documentation that tied things to King. He reached out to King, and then the author called him and admitted it before revealing it to the world and killing off his pseudonym.

Thinner remains an underseen Stephen King adaptation. Robert John Burke played Billy Halleck, but there were some more familiar faces in the cast. These included Joe Mantegna as the Mafia boss. It was also directed by a big-time director, Tom Holland, who had also directed the King miniseries The Langoliers and was the man who directed and co-wrote the original Child's Play movie and wrote and directed the cult vampire film Fright Night . However, Thinner wasn't reviewed well and did poorly at the box office.

However, there are other Richard Bachman adaptations that have been received more favorably, including two King movies released in 2025. The first Richard Bachman adaptation was The Running Man in 1987, an Arnold Schwarzenegger movie in which he starred as a man forced to play a deadly game on reality television for his freedom. That is also where Bachman's books are becoming popular again. In 2025, The Running Man was remade, and a second Bachman story, The Long Walk , was released after years of fans demanding its arrival on the big screen. If anything, it proves what King wanted fans to know. He was more than just horror, even if it was a horror story that outed his secret.

What are your thoughts on Stephen King's Richard Bachman books? Let us know your favorite of these in the comments below.

articles.title: How Amin Joseph Brought "Humanity" to Sonny Liston in 'The Greatest'
articles.summary: Amazon's Muhammad Ali series rewrites history for one of boxing's biggest heels.
articles.content:
Sonny Liston stood 6'1″ and, in his prime, weighed in at 218 pounds. For Prime Video 's The Greatest , actor Amin Joseph ( Snowfall ) added the requisite 23 pounds to his 6'1 (and ½"!) frame to perfectly match that of the former champ.

Joseph proved to be a solid facsimile of Liston in other ways, too. For one, he can really throw hands.

"I grew up fighting," Joseph told The Hollywood Reporter . "My dad got me into boxing when I was probably around 8 or 9."

It was probably no coincidence that the formal lessons began shortly after the family moved to Harlem. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Deborah Ann Woll to Reprise 'God of War' Role in Prime Video Series TV Melania Trump Stresses Humanitarian Efforts at Chic Premiere for Two-Episode Series Documentary Follow-Up

Either way, it stuck, and Joseph would box on and off into his college years studying theatre at Howard University. The natural southpaw (not that he told production before landing the role — Liston was a righty) says he had a "knack" for the violent sport, but ultimately was unwilling or unable to "slave [his] mind over" to a coach.

"If he says, 'Run through a wall.' If he says, 'Eat sheetrock' — you need to slave your mind over to that process," Joseph said. "[My coach] saw that I already had self-confidence and that I was already shaped as a young man in a certain way, and it was just not worth the investment (for him)."

Boxing is a sport built on length, speed, power, mental fortitude, and in many cases, having an absent (or at least shitty) father. With a present dad at home, Joseph was not looking for what so many younger fighters subconsciously seek. His training had logical limits.

"If [a trainer says], 'Run at 3 in the morning when it's raining,' you don't need someone going, 'Well, wait a minute — is that the smartest thing?'" Joseph explained. "You need someone that goes, 'I'm running.' Because it could be life or death if you're in the ring and [a coach] says, 'I need you to throw this combo.'" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The coach needs the fighter to throw that combo and never question his corner. Joseph, who describes himself as "a thespian through and through," always saw past the ring.

Liston, for better or worse, was a boxing coach's dream. Born into a poor sharecropping family, Liston was uneducated and basically tortured by his father. As a young teenager, he ran away from their Arkansas plantation and toward the streets of St. Louis, Missouri. By his early 20s (Liston never really knew his age), Liston was incarcerated.

Not that he minded much: inmates get three meals a day, every single day.

Liston "wanted to be accepted" like "a child" does, Joseph said. So he did as he was told. It was not a lifetime of great advice.

It was in the Missouri State Penitentiary that Liston found boxing. Or really, it was boxing that found Liston. Once more, that would be for better (he'd become World Heavyweight Champion in 1962) and for worse (Liston died under suspicious circumstances in 1970). Throughout his career, Liston was surrounded by unsavory characters.

Before reading Ben Watkins' scripts, Joseph didn't know more about Liston than your average… Joseph. He was tangentially aware of the man from the below-pictured infamous KO, which lived on as a mural on the wall of Joseph's boxing gym (and surely hundreds of others).

Joseph got the education needed from those scripts. He also gained the confidence that he'd have the appropriate screen time to show Liston's "thought process," as well as his "humility" and "humbleness." It is Joseph's quietest moments in the series that speak the loudest to viewers — not an easy task when playing opposite the loudest and most relentless talker in boxing history. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

(Cassius Clay/Muhammad Ali was portrayed with trademark bravado by Jaalen Best. Yes, "Best" was "The Greatest" in what THR TV critic Daniel Fienberg called "a star-making performance." Fienberg said Joseph "makes Liston into a flawed but tragic figure, ferocious in the ring but eager to find acceptance outside of it," and calls Liston/Joseph's talk show-appearance scene "one of the series’ highlights.")

As heavy as Joseph's new (pure muscle) weight was, what weighed most on the real Liston was "the shame" of being illiterate throughout adulthood, Joseph said. For Joseph, the greatest selling point of The Greatest is that Watkins doesn't portray Liston as "a dimwit," as the media of the time certainly did.

"Literacy isn't a direct correlation to your intelligence," Joseph said. "[Liston] is a man that moves in the silence, but when he does talk, it's so poignant."

All episodes of The Greatest are currently available on Amazon Prime Video.

Inter Alia, the previewing production of Suzie Miller's new play starring Rosamund Pike, seems about to repeat its London success here on Broadway , with the first seven-performance week selling out and grossing $993,103 .

The play (opening at the Music Box Theatre on December 1) was one of the stronger performers on Broadway for the week ending November 22, along with other sell-outs A Few Good Men, Hamilton, Much Ado About Nothing , Other Desert Cities and, in its final week, The Imaginary Invalid starring Bill Irwin (grossing $599,290 ).

Top earner was, far and away, Hamilton , with Christopher Jackson back in the role of George Washington (through January 3), sending box office soaring to $3,039,502 . Closest runner up was Other Desert Cities at $2,562,632 . Other Desert Cities, with Julia Louis-Dreyfuss leading a cast that includes Ed Harris, Allison Janney, Joe Keery and Lily Rabe, was, as usual, the priciest Broadway option, with an average ticket price of a whopping $328.88 . Another recent arrival of the fall season, the acclaimed Here There Are Blueberries , had an excellent week at the Barrymore, grossing $1,035,188 and filling 99% of seats. Much Ado About Nothing , starring Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell, continued doing gangbusters, grossing $2,073,288 for its opening week, even with press tickets and opening night comps.

T he Fantasticks , at the Hayes in a production by the nonprofit Second Stage, grossed $375,151, filling 95% of the seats.

Galileo had a fairly rough week at the Shubert, with star Raúl Esparza missing four performances due to a concussion suffered during a rehearsal (he returned to the show Friday, November 20). A few specialty, holiday-season productions pulled so-so crowds last week, with the magic-illusion show Now You See Me Live selling about 77% of seats at the Hirschfeld for a gross of $648,118 , while Blue Man Group's A New Holiday Surprise opened at the Lunt-Fontanne on November 17, filling 60% of seats for the week at a modest average ticket price of $44.36 and an equally slim $317,376 gross. It's A Wonderful Life: A Live Radio Play , in previews at the Broadhurst (it opened last night following a November 18 gala performance) sold about 76% of available seats for a $457,581 gross.

Chicago grossed $1,182,400 for the week, donating net proceeds from the 30th anniversary Monday performance to the Entertainment Community Fund. And Buena Vista Social Club took in $917,221 , filling 96% of seats at the Schoenfeld and announcing that former New York Yankees player-turned-musician Bernie Williams will be extending his limited engagement in the show through the end of the musical's run on January 17, 2027.

In all, the 38 Broadway productions grossed a total $40,374,391 for the week ending November 22, about the same as the previous week and even with last year at this time. Attendance was 313,587 , down 2% from the previous week but up 8% year-to-year.

In the 26th week of the 2026-27 season, Broadway has grossed $843,441,665 season-to-date, down about 7% from last year at this time, with total attendance of 6,853,368 down 2% year-to-year.

It is as yet unknown if she will have a series regular or recurring role.

articles.title: Marvel Confirms Patrick Stewart Was Offered a Role in Avengers: Secret Wars
articles.summary: Marvel Avengers: Doomsday will be a major Marvel movie milestone in so many ways, and not all of them will be fantastical; some of them will be heartbreaking in a very real and painful way. For a long time, we thought that one of the biggest tugs on our heartstrings would be seeing actors Patrick Stewart […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday will be a major Marvel movie milestone in so many ways, and not all of them will be fantastical; some of them will be heartbreaking in a very real and painful way. For a long time, we thought that one of the biggest tugs on our heartstrings would be seeing actors Patrick Stewart and Ian McKellen onscreen together as X-Men's Professor X and Magneto, one last time. However, the recent death of Patrick Stewart has changed that fundamentally, as Avengers: Doomsday will now serve as Stewart's final screen performance .

With Patrick Stewart gone, obviously his version of Charles Xavier will also end with Avengers: Doomsday . But apparently that wasn't the case originally.

Marvel Studios offered Stewart a role in Avengers: Secret Wars , seeing Xavier as the unwavering "conscience" guiding the heroes through the multiversal war, according to director Joe Russo. However, it was Stewart who turned down the offer, preferring to have a role only in Avengers: Doomsday .

Based on Joe Russo's full description, it doesn't sound like Xavier will have a big role in Avengers: Doomsday ; that said, it also sounds like Stewart made good use of every moment he was onscreen. "He has a lovely scene with Ian McKellen, who’s his best friend [Magneto], in the film," Russo explained. "It’s a very emotional scene about forgiveness, and I think very resonant in the wake of his passing."

It's also somewhat haunting to hear The Russos and Marvel Studios head Kevin Feige recall the almost prescient sense of finality both they and Stewart felt on his last day of filming. While no one knew it would be Patrick Stewart's final day ever on a film set – but somehow, they also kind of did .

“He stood up, and he gave a speech to the crew,” Kevin Feige shared. “We didn’t know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was.”

“I think it was in the back of all of our heads: we may never see him on set again,” Anthony Russo added, saying the whole experience was “Very emotional."

That emotion was only heightened by the fact that Patrick Stewart was already showing visible signs of poor health while filming Avengers: Doomsday . "It was clear that he was struggling with his health, and he worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence — for us as directors, for his other actors, for the crew," Anthony Russo shared. "You could see it wasn’t just the effort of a regular actor showing up and delivering that kind of presence and performance and experience for others, collaboration. It was someone who was really being challenged in a very deep way on a health level, showing up and doing that. For him to have muscled through and delivered the performance that he did in that movie, and the experience that he delivered for all of us as collaborators, it made it intensely emotional.”

Avengers: Doomsday will be in theaters on December 18th.

Steven Hack, the theater veteran who spent five years on Broadway as an original castmember in Cats , then appeared as a character actor in dozens of films and TV shows, has died. He was 68.

Hack died Thursday at home following what was described as “a sudden and unexpected cardiac event,” the Interact Theatre Company announced . He was a founding member of the North Hollywood-based group that launched in 1989.

“Steven was a gifted and versatile performer, a superb graphic artist and a cherished member of our artistic family,” ITC directors Barry Heins and Walter Ware said in a statement. “His creativity and talent helped shape Interact in its earliest years, and his artistry, humor, warmth and generous spirit enriched everything he touched.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Lifestyle The Pulitzer-Winning Play 'Purpose' Finally Came to Los Angeles. Born in St. Louis on April 20, 1958, Hack studied at CalArts and The American Academy of Dramatic Arts in Los Angeles. In 1978, he was a background dancer in the film version of Grease and appeared in the off-Broadway musical The Coolest Cat in Town .

Hack was there when Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Cats opened at the Winter Garden Theatre on Oct. 7, 1982, and he portrayed several characters, including Coricopat, Mungojerrie, Carbucketty, Tumblebrutus and Pouncival, over the next five years.

He toured with Michael Bennett’s A Chorus Line for nearly two years and then joined the Broadway production at the Shubert Theatre for one show only — its record-breaking 3,389th Great White Way performance on Sept. 29, 1983. (He did Cats that night, too.)

articles.title: 5 Best Non-Superhero Comics Going Today and 1 Is Being Made Into a Movie
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Image Comics Some of the best comics being published today have nothing to do with Marvel Comics and DC superheroes, with some examples being horror titles about a zombie whose heart starts beating again, several killers set loose in a small town on Halloween, or an entire title centered around conspiracy theories. While superhero comics dominate the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Some of the best comics being published today have nothing to do with Marvel Comics and DC superheroes, with some examples being horror titles about a zombie whose heart starts beating again, several killers set loose in a small town on Halloween, or an entire title centered around conspiracy theories. While superhero comics dominate the sales charts, there are a lot of creator-owned titles and imprint horror, sci-fi, and fantasy stories that people are talking about today. Image Comics remains the core publisher for many of these titles, but it isn't the only company that pushes these non-superhero books.

There are some big-time creators working in this space today, including James Tynion IV and Deniz Camp, and they are proving that great stories can have nothing to do with superheroes and still stand tall above even tales about men in capes. Some of these books are even new enough that you can catch up on them now without digging into years of backstory. One of these stories is even big enough that it is in development to become a Hollywood movie.

Bleeding Hearts is a Vertigo series, the first new title from the DC Vertigo relaunch . The first issue went on sale in February 2026, and there have been nine issues released to date for the series. Bleeding Hearts is a series by Deniz Camp and Stipan Morian that follows a zombie named Poke whose heart starts beating again. The world in the comics is quirky, with the zombies actually having an intelligence and talking to each other, but still having an insatiable desire to eat the living.

The story is set about 10 years after humanity falls, when zombies are the dominant life form. The twist comes at the start, when Poke's heart starts beating again, and he sees the living as friends instead of food, which is a problem since he is now in the minority, and the other zombies don't take kindly to his new feelings. Later issues add human survivors, and the series remains one of the most original and quirky zombie stories going today.

The Department of Truth is an Image Comics series by James Tynion IV and Martin Simmonds that launched in 2020. It is still ongoing to this day, with issue #39 starting a new story arc. The story follows FBI agent Cole Turner, who learns that conspiracy theories are real and is pulled into a battle to decide reality for every person on Earth. In the series, the Department of Truth is nothing new, and it traces back to beliefs recorded by Pope Sylvester II in 1000 A.D.

The book has a high-concept premise, with the idea that if enough people believe in a conspiracy theory, myth, or alternate fact, it can manifest itself into existence, or even rewrite reality. The comics have a secret government agency bring in Turner to stop dangerous ideas from coming into existence, while there are rival forces that fight to shape what the world will turn into if they are successful. Tynion brings in several real-world theories, from JFK's assassination and the Satanic Panic to things like Bigfoot, making this a smart, surreal, and entertaining read.

Crowbound is a new Image Comics series from Jeff Lemire ( Sweet Tooth ) and Dustin Nguyen ( Little Monsters ). The first issue went on sale in September 2026, and it is already earning great reviews, which should come as no surprise for Lemire. There have only been three issues so far, but this series is already a fantastic story, and it can only go up from here. This is a post-apocalyptic dark fantasy where children start working in the Factory at age 13. They work to help maintain a wall to keep an alien being known as the Eater out, and are ruled by evil men who have taken over as the ruling class.

However, everything changes when a woman named Rose has her daughter taken away a year before the girl turns 13 and is killed trying to save her. Rose then returns from the dead, now bound to an ancient spirit known as the Scarecrow Queen, and she sets out to save her daughter and free her people before a man connected to an evil being can stop her. This is a dark and disturbing story that is one of the most promising books available today.

Assorted Crisis Events is an Image Comics series by Deniz Camp and Eric Zawadzki that started publication in 2025. This ongoing series has nine issues so far and is an anthology comic book series set in a world where time is unraveling, with each issue following a new character and a figure called the Broken Man appearing in every issue. The series is a sci-fi high-concept idea with a reality where time is collapsing, and the past, present, and future make it hard to keep track of what is going on. However, each issue has normal people experiencing the phenomenon and shows how it affects their real lives.

This series mixes apocalyptic events, time loops, dinosaurs from the past, robots from the future, and even displaced historical figures, and shows how regular people deal with it all. There is also a strong sense of how modern-day crises weigh on people, with looks at trauma, memory loss, relentless disasters in the news, and economic pressures breaking down society. It is one of the most experimental and thought-provoking comics being published today.

Exquisite Corpses is an Image Comics series co-created by James Tynion IV and Michael Walsh. The series is an action-horror story with a dozen killers dropped into a small town on Halloween with the instructions to kill each other. Each killer was chosen by 12 of the 13 wealthy families who control everything (the family hosting the event doesn't get a killer to compete), and whichever killer survives gives the family that hired him leadership for the next five years. However, in this series, there are people in the town who fight back.

The first season ran 13 issues and ended in May 2026, but three of the killers got spin-off comics. There is a sequel that will take place in a new town and is set to arrive in 2027. The series has proven to be so successful that it is being developed into a movie by Blumhouse Atomic, although there is no word on a director yet. While the first season is over, the spin-offs added more stories, and a second season will continue the comic series, making this a perfect non-superhero comic book for anyone who loves blood-soaked action.

What is your favorite current non-superhero comic book series? Let us know any we might have missed in the comments below.

articles.title: The Pulitzer-Winning Play 'Purpose' Finally Came to Los Angeles. But That Doesn't Mean It's Gone Hollywood.
articles.summary: Branden Jacobs-Jenkins reunites the entire company, including Kara Young and director Phylicia Rashad, for a sold-out run at the Geffen Playhouse.
articles.content:
Branden Jacobs-Jenkins is, famously, a tinkerer. His plays go through long, thoughtful development processes. He first wrote Appropriate a decade before it became the 2024 Tony Award-winning play starring Sarah Paulson. His next work, Purpose , went through a nuanced workshop with the actors before it premiered at the Steppenwolf Theatre in Chicago; the company finalized the ending one day before the first performance. "They were walking on stage with pages in hand, that's how fresh it was," says Jacobs-Jenkins. "But they say the great writers all rewrite — Arthur Miller was rewriting his plays at the end of his life. Shakespeare obviously was rewriting King Lear over and over again." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Lifestyle 'The Comedy About Spies' to Open on Broadway This Spring Lifestyle 'Birthright,' About Differing Attitudes on Israel, Set For Broadway

Director Phylicia Rashad is quick to point out that she sees Jacobs-Jenkins' process as a gift, noting how rare it is for a company to have success access to the playwright during rehearsals. "I've only had this experience once before, with August Wilson and Gem of the Ocean ," she says. "The first production I did was here in Los Angeles at the Mark Taper forum, and then it went to the Huntington in Boston and eventually to Broadway — he continued to refine that play until we opened on Broadway, and I loved it." Plus, she adds of Jacobs-Jenkins, "You cannot tell a playwright, this genius, 'You have got to have this by three o'clock tomorrow.' That doesn't work."

Purpose eventually transferred to Broadway, where it won best play and best performance by an actress in a featured role (for Kara Young ), as well as the 2025 Pulitzer Prize for drama. But Jacobs-Jenkins says that despite the accolades he still hopes to polish it until the bitter end. "Every time I hear the play I think: I want to change this or that," he laughs. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The storied stage play, which centers on a politically dynastic Black family (not entirely unlike that of the Reverend Jesse Jackson) during a dinner welcoming their eldest home from his white collar crime prison stint, is now in the midst of a revival at Los Angeles' Geffen Playhouse . The entire Broadway cast, along with Rashad, reunited for the L.A. run, an occasion that proved both historic and also tempting for a playwright who loves the chance to revisit his work. "I actually felt a lot of pressure to leave it alone, because so many people want to see the Broadway production," he says. "So I can't just be out here messing with the thing. I don't want to rock the boat."

Here, Jacobs-Jenkins tells THR about what it's like to bring a piece of theater to a famously screen-forward town.

When you wrote Purpose , did you imagine it would have as much success as it did?

That's the thing, is that I really try to keep myself in check because I can get a little wild. I try to fight the fire right in front of me. I had this commission from the Steppenwolf Theater Company to write a play, and Alana Arenas is this incredible actor at the company and honestly my wildest dream was to bring her to Broadway. She plays Morgan in Purpose , and she's one of those people that if you know her you're obsessed with her. So I was like, I'm about to bring her to New York. And I got to do that, which is crazy. But the truth is I wanted to make something with people I like. And for whatever reason, whenever I do something with that in mind, it does keep going. If I'm launching something with some ambition, it's always falling apart, but if a project starts with the people they go the furthest. I've learned that lesson. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Purpose first played for audiences in Chicago, and then New York. Does it feel at all formidable to come to an industry town?

I've had some great experiences in L.A. with theater, honestly. My play Gloria happened here and did pretty well. And Appropriate played at the Mark Taper Forum. It's not a theater town, but it is an actor town. Anytime I've done a show here, the cast has been absolutely incredible. The audiences weren't necessarily the most full, but the people who were there were theatergoers. For me, theater has to be a celebration of the actor. These people go out there, they're not hiding behind a cut, they're not hiding behind coverage. They're like athletes and they're telling you a story in real time without a break. In Chicago, audiences are very sophisticated, they have a high bar for writing because they're the city of David Mamet, they're the city of Tracy Letts. L.A. has a similar vibe, but also… I don't know how to go down this road though, I'm not trying to say anything spicy. I would say there can be a dismissiveness of theater, because when you see the kind of capital that moves through television and film, the company town energy can take over. Even though theater could be the most impactful, powerful experience of your life, nobody is counting box office.

How much pressure do you feel towards writing screenplays or putting your stage work up for adaptation? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I would never adapt my own plays to movies or film, but I do love those mediums and I've dabbled in both with varying degrees of success. Like most playwrights, I've been feeding myself with some screen work for quite some time now. I'm a proud member of the WGA-East. But I know that I can do whatever I want in a play and I don't have to beg some executive to let me do. I never have to ask for permission to execute my ideas. That freedom is so necessary to me as an artist. It's funny, some of the most powerful directors and showrunners I know have said they're jealous of my work and I'm like, what the fuck are you talking about? But it's because we're all just writers who want to be able to execute our visions — and there's less red tape in the theater.

But you could also pass off the adapting, and the dealing with red tape, to someone else…

I think a lot of hit plays and musicals that have been turned into movies and they just don't hit the same way. And I don't want to get blamed for that. So if somebody else came along trying to do it, I'm here to support them. If they win, I win. Tennessee Williams never adapted his own scripts — the smartest thing he did was be like, I'm going to sit back and take this check, but I hope y'all have a good time. That being said, I feel like people do make the mistake of thinking these forms are more similar than they are. The pleasures are very different.

You know they're developing The Invite for Broadway, right? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Did no one learn anything from Dog Day Afternoon ? Why would someone pay a premium to see a play when they can go home and see the movie that they already know is really good. I mean, let me stop. I should not talk smack about it, but it does make me think, what ? I would love it if they would just bankroll a new play. There have been several hit movies and TV shows lately that people have said, oh it's so good, it's like a play. Like Adolescence , when everyone was like, "Oh my God, they're acting in real time." And people who do plays are like, "Yeah we do that every night. What are you guys freaking out about?" Come see a play. If your vibe is two couples in an apartment, I have so many good plays for you.

What's the latest with your next play?

We've been developing Grass for two years, we had a great workshop last September, and we start rehearsals in two months. We just got a cast together, and it's going to star Daniel Kaluuya.

I'm sure you saw his hit on the local Oregon news during the FAA shutdown?

I got so many texts about him. He has responsibilities, he was on his way somewhere special, okay? ( Laughs .) I'm glad he's back on the news for whatever reasons.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Rockstar Games has spent years establishing Grand Theft Auto as one of the most ambitious open-world franchises in gaming, and nothing proves this more than Grand Theft Auto 6 . Its open world even surpasses that of Grand Theft Auto 5 . The latest entry pushes the series so much further in many ways. However, there is a major area where Rockstar Games have completely failed, and by removing this popular GTA 5 feature, it could be a sign of something terrible to come and could shape GTA 6's legacy going forward.

Buying vehicles might not sound like an essential feature in a series built around stealing them, but it has become an important part of the Grand Theft Auto experience. There is something satisfying about saving money, purchasing an expensive sports car, and taking it for a drive. It gives players another reason to earn money beyond what the story requires. Removing that freedom from GTA 6 raises questions about why Rockstar would abandon an established feature. More concerning is what this decision could suggest about the developer's plans for GTA 6 Online and its approach to monetization moving forward.

One of the best parts of finishing the campaign in GTA 5 was having millions of dollars to spend however you wanted in complete free roam. I blew through so much money filling out my garages and racing through Los Santos. The same was true for boats, planes, and helicopters. Rockstar even expanded these selections through updates, adding vehicles like the Pegassi Osiris and Buckingham Luxor Deluxe to the single-player experience. Purchasing vehicles gave players something to work toward outside the main story.

Unfortunately, GTA 6 handles vehicle ownership considerably differently. Rather than purchasing cars through dealerships or websites, players generally need to steal vehicles and pay to register them as personal vehicles . There are scripted opportunities to get cars throughout the narrative; freely browsing and purchasing them is not an option. It is even worse for planes, helicopters, and boats, as you cannot actually register them permanently and only keep them as long as you have fuel or until you lose them.

One could argue this makes for Jason and Lucia's "Rags-to-riches" story, and hunting down rare vehicles does encourage exploration. But there is no reason this system couldn't coexist with being able to purchase vehicles. Rockstar could have introduced its new registration mechanics while retaining traditional vehicle purchases, giving players greater freedom over how they build their collections. This feels like a major step back and could have heavy implications for GTA 6's future.

Considering the success of GTA Online , it's difficult not to question whether Rockstar is reserving vehicle purchases for the multiplayer component of GTA 6 . Buying vehicles is one of the driving factors of its online experience. Over the years, players have gained access to everything from flying motorcycles and weaponized supercars to military aircraft and submarines. Of course, none of these were added to the single-player campaign, even if players could purchase standard vehicles. With this in mind, it makes me worried about how Rockstar will handle this in GTA 6 Online .

Another problem is how expensive purchasing vehicles in GTA Online was. Players often needed to dedicate hours to completing heists, operating businesses, and repeating activities to afford desirable additions to their garages. Alternatively, Rockstar offered Shark Cards, allowing players to purchase in-game currency with real money. This forced players to either grind cash or spend real cash to get the vehicles they want. The pricing on these cards was ridiculous, even by microtransaction standards, and players could be in real trouble depending on how GTA 6 handles this.

If GTA 6 Online follows a similar model, removing vehicle purchases from single-player could make multiplayer the only place players can enjoy traditional vehicle collecting. I wouldn't be surprised if this was intentional, and if this signals that players will be facing even more expensive Shark Cards or longer grinds. Rockstar hasn't confirmed that monetization influenced this particular design decision, but its history with GTA Online makes the possibility concerning, to say the least. Considering the time and resources poured into GTA 6 , its realism, and attention to detail, the cost could be more than what players expect.

What makes this omission particularly frustrating is how much effort Rockstar has put into making GTA 6 feel alive. The world practically begs players to explore every corner, experiment with its systems, and develop their own playstyles. Part of that should have been purchasing an expensive yacht, earning a private jet, or cruising through Leonida in a fancy car customized to your every wish. These are natural additions to an open-world game that emphasizes immersion, and without them, player freedom is limited, and there is very little to actually spend in-game money on , especially near the end of GTA 6's narrative.

One of my favorite things about open-world games is reaching a point where money no longer dictates every decision. The appeal shifts from survival and progression to enjoying the rewards of everything I have done. GTA 5 understood this perfectly. Purchasing an expensive supercar wasn't always practical, but practicality wasn't the point. It was about enjoying the freedom that came with completing the campaign and establishing yourself within its world. This isn't possible in GTA 6 , at least not in the single-player campaign.

Rockstar has created an incredible world with GTA 6, but it is so disappointing that we are limited in how we explore it. Rockstar could still add dealerships and ways to purchase vehicles in an update, but it feels like a weird oversight not to include it from the start if the studio goes this route. This makes me think GTA 6 Online is where this comes in, but players shouldn't have to enter multiplayer experiences or deal with excessive grinding and microtransactions to enjoy features in past games. It remains to be seen how Rockstar handles GTA 6 Online , but my expectations are low based on the decision to cut one of GTA 5's best features.

articles.title: Netflix Buys Radford Studio Lot for $380 Million
articles.summary: The purchase gives the entertainment giant ownership of a major Los Angeles production campus.
articles.content:
Netflix is buying Radford Studio Center for $380 million, taking ownership of one of Hollywood's most storied production lots as the entertainment giant expands its physical footprint in Los Angeles.

The deal, which is expected to close on Tuesday, follows an auction during which the property's lender took back the property after Hackman Capital Partners defaulted on its mortgage amid historically low production levels in the region. Netflix reached an agreement with the Goldman Sachs-led lender to acquire the lot. The company also paid

The $380 million price point is roughly 20 percent of the $1.85 billion Hackman Capital paid for Radford in 2021, a massive repricing of a legacy Hollywood lot and indicative of the flight of filming away from Los Angeles and California.

After it took over the property, Goldman handled the foreclosure to facilitate a sale. As part of the deal, Netflix paid the so-called mansion tax, which imposes a 5.5 percent levy for properties valued above $10.9 million.

As part of the deal, Netflix has pacted with Louis Dargenzio’s rising studio services firm Zello, contracting with its entertainment advisory division ZVantage to manage the transition as well as partnering with Dargenzio’s production equipment provider Cinelease to provide services. (Cinelease is a rival to Quixote, which is owned by the studio services giant Hudson Pacific that Netflix currently leases from at Sunset Studios.)

In a memo to staff, Netflix said that it purchased Radford to "strengthen our investment in Los Angeles and California."

"This city is home to us," it said. "We’re excited to keep investing here and finding more ways to entertain the world, while supporting the writers, builders, electricians, drivers, designers, and talent who make L.A., California, and the entertainment industry so special."

Ted Sarandos has never hid his love for Old Hollywood, and now the Netflix co-CEO owns a 55-acre and 98-year old piece of Tinseltown property.

After months of negotiations, speculation and reporting by Deadline that things were moving ahead, Netflix has bought the iconic Radford Studio Center in Studio City. The anticipated auction of the property today proved a bit of a non-event as Goldman Sachs-led lenders pulled the lot back and sold it directly to the streamer.

With 1,000 Netflix employees let go last month, execs such as Content chief Bela Bajaria ousted last month, dissent among the ranks , and the stock still struggling, the optics around such a big outlay of cash might not look so good. But this is Hollywood, where perception is reality and the Sarandos and Greg Peters-led streamer is leaning into a narrative of being good industry citizens in today's purchase to give some gloss to the whole thing.

"There’s still a long way to go, but we are hopeful that with the partnership of the State of California and the City of Los Angeles, this will be the start of a meaningful new investment in California's film industry," Netflix said today of the purchase and the future it envisions for Radford as a production hub in what has been some very tough times for the home of Hollywood the past five years.

With facilities in various states of readiness in New Mexico, plus tax credits rich New York and New Jersey, the streamer Tuesday went full Randy Newman about L.A.

"This city is home to us," they exclaimed. "We’re excited to keep investing here and finding more ways to entertain the world, while supporting the writers, builders, electricians, drivers, designers, and talent who make L.A., California, and the entertainment industry so special."

To the over 50,000 industry workers who have seen their jobs disappear since 2020 that can't help but sound like hope. The statement (see the full missive below) also can't help but remind some of the threats to leave L.A. that Skydance were leaking like crazy in its ultimately successful effort to seal the $111 billion merger of Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery earlier this summer. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Having said that, nothing's gonna change for a while at either Netflix's Sunset Blvd leased HQ or for the current renters at the former CBS hub Sticking to their current leases, the streamer plans to stay at the Hollywood locations until around 2032. As for those already at Radford, a source close to the situation tells me that "business will continue as usual on the lot in the near term, including for productions that are currently filming on the lot."

Business as usual, in an ever changing business — and Ted got his lot.

Read the full statement from Netflix on the purchase Of Radford Studio Center here:

Unless you work in entertainment or live in Los Angeles, you may not have heard of Radford Studio Center. But you’ve probably seen something that was made there.

Opened in 1928, at the end of the silent film era, Radford has been home to a long list of classic shows — from Gunsmoke and Gilligan's Island to The Mary Tyler Moore Show, Seinfeld, and That ‘70s Show, among many, many others.

Today, we’re proud to share that Netflix is purchasing Radford to build on that history and strengthen our investment in Los Angeles and California.

Netflix was founded in California, and we opened our first office in L.A. more than two decades ago. Since then, many of our shows like early favorites Grace and Frankie and GLOW have filmed in L.A., as have more recent series and films like Nobody Wants This, The Lincoln Lawyer , The Rip and The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth . This year alone, more than 45 of our shows and movies are confirmed to film across L.A.

We’ve also engaged ZVantage, Zello’s entertainment advisory division, to support the transition and next chapter of the iconic lot through its operating platform, Backlot Studio Services. As part of the engagement, Cinelease will serve as a production equipment provider at the studio, further enhancing the infrastructure and services available to the production community. Working together, our goal is to maintain operational continuity, retain the existing studio team and strengthen Radford’s position as a premier production destination.

There’s still a long way to go, but we are hopeful that with the partnership of the State of California and the City of Los Angeles, this will be the start of a meaningful new investment in California's film industry.

This city is home to us. We’re excited to keep investing here and finding more ways to entertain the world, while supporting the writers, builders, electricians, drivers, designers, and talent who make L.A., California, and the entertainment industry so special.

articles.title: Forgotten 1960s Shonen Classic Is Now Easier to Stream in the U.S. Than Ever
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Tatsunoko Production Criterion is streaming one of the most iconic 1960s anime series that have been forgotten over the decades due to limitations in access. The history of the anime industry dates back several decades, but the medium finally began becoming popular in Japan during the 1950s and 1960s, thanks to the color theatrical features and the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Criterion is streaming one of the most iconic 1960s anime series that have been forgotten over the decades due to limitations in access. The history of the anime industry dates back several decades, but the medium finally began becoming popular in Japan during the 1950s and 1960s, thanks to the color theatrical features and the rise of TV animation. Several classics across all demographics were released during that era, and it goes without saying that Shonen was more popular than others even back then. However, while those series were pretty popular during the time of their broadcast, most of them couldn't stand the test of time when it became increasingly difficult for fans to watch them later on.

This is especially true for fans in the U.S. since several older classics are difficult to watch even now. However, Criterion made it possible to stream Speed Racer , one of the most legendary anime shows of all time. While it isn't an obscure show anymore, thanks to the Hollywood live-action adaptation by the Wachowski sisters in 2008, the anime itself has been difficult to watch for a while now. The official Instagram handle of the service revealed its December 2026 lineup, where Speed Racer was also listed. The handle confirms that the complete series will be available on the platform in both Japanese audio with subtitles and the English dub as well.

Based on an iconic manga written and illustrated by Tatsuo Yoshida, Speed Racer premiered in 1967 and ran for 52 episodes. The story centers around Go Mifune, who pilots the Mach 5, the name of the technologically advanced racing car built by his father, Pops Racer. The series doesn't shy away from portraying the brutality of the world of professional racing as Go gets entangled with all kinds of underhanded plots of corrupt businessmen and obstacles set by his rivals.

The visuals and color palette might give the impression that it's a kid's show, but it handles mature themes that are suitable for viewers of all ages. Not to mention that the best part of the anime was that, unlike typical racing stories, it blends family drama, political intrigue, and automotive fantasy.

Established in 1962, Tatsunoko Production eventually became one of the oldest animation studios in Japan that's relevant to this day. Over the decades, the animation studio has released more than 200 anime, including films and series. It's known for several acclaimed shows, such as Ping Pong the Animation , Psycho-Pass , and many more.

The studio thrived during the 1970s and 1980s, when there wasn’t an endless stream of anime TV shows being released for global fans. However, its legacy is mostly thanks to the success of Speed Racer , which helped the studio gain a strong foothold in the industry not long after its establishment. The studio even released a reboot and spin-off in an attempt to keep this series relevant for the next few decades.

Have you heard of Speed Racer before? Head down to the comments to let us know if you will be watching the anime next month on Criterion.

articles.title: Why Is Avengers: Doomsday Missing Key X-Men? Directors Address Absence of Storm & Rogue
articles.summary: Why is Avengers: Doomsday missing some of the most iconic Fox X-Men stars like Halle Berry and Anna Paquin? Ever since the cast for the new MCU movie was confirmed to include a slew of heavy hitters from the franchise making their return, the glaring absence of some major names was one of the hottest […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Why is Avengers: Doomsday missing some of the most iconic Fox X-Men stars like Halle Berry and Anna Paquin? Ever since the cast for the new MCU movie was confirmed to include a slew of heavy hitters from the franchise making their return , the glaring absence of some major names was one of the hottest topics of discussion for Marvel fans. Even though Hugh Jackman wasn't part of the original line-up, it's essentially been confirmed that he'll appear , but characters like Storm, Rogue, even Jean Grey and Iceman don't seem to be part of the film's plans.

Speaking with Entertainment Weekly in a new interview, Avengers: Doomsday directors Joe and Anthony Russo addressed the absence of these fixtures from the Fox X-Men movies. Though the pair wouldn't explain exactly why certain stars weren't invited back, Joe Russo told the outlet the X-Men casting “was really targeted. It was really specific.” Anthony took it a step further, revealing that their choices for the X-Men in Doomsday stretched back to their film history , a point that will only make some fans keep questioning.

According to Anthony Russo, the X-Men characters that were selected were done so because of their history on the big screen, with the team considering how their stories had played out already across the X-Men films and what it would mean for them to witness the destruction of it all with Doomsday 's incursions.

“We really do have a process where we see the entire film through each character’s eyes, no matter what the size of their role is,” Anthony added. “With the X-Men, we got to really deep dive and think about their histories as characters, their experiences, and how this particular moment in time was gonna affect them. There’s such a rich history to them that we really do bring them to the film as if it’s their movie, as well.”

The reasoning is sound from Russo, but it begs the question why a cataclysmic event like this wouldn't be something noteworthy for the likes of Paquin's Rogue or Berry's Storm. Both characters were part of the Fox X-Men movies from the beginning, with the former event being largely cut from her triumphant return in X-Men: Days of Future Past . If anything, the explanation from the Russos about why certain X-Men characters aren't on the team in Doomsday only makes their absence more obvious, and that's without even considering other stars.

All that in mind, it's very possible that one reason some of these X-Men stars weren't tapped for Avengers: Doomsday is because Marvel has something else in mind for them, maybe even an appearance in Avengers: Secret Wars . At this point, any talk of the MCU's 2027 movie feels like a pipe dream, as production has been pushed into next year. That said, it wouldn't be out of the question for other X-Men favorites to return, Berry's Storm being a part of the Thor Corps on Battleworld feels like the kind of image Kevin Feige dreams about. Hopefully the opening of Doomsday doesn't indicate that they've already been taken off the board in some fashion

articles.title: Kevin Kline Boards 'The Corrections' at Netflix
articles.summary: He'll star opposite Meryl Streep in the adaptation of Jonathan Franzen's novel.
articles.content:
Netflix is adding a second Oscar winner to the cast of The Corrections .

Kevin Kline will star opposite Meryl Streep in the limited series adaptation of Jonathan Franzen's novel. The series will be an on-screen reunion for Kline and Streep, who have appeared together in the feature films Sophie's Choice (Kline's film debut), A Prairie Home Companion and Ricki and the Flash .

articles.title: ‘The Spiral’ Director Paolo Strippoli Talks Oscar-Buzzed Horror Pic: “I Try to Lower Expectations”
articles.summary: The filmmaker has momentum but acknowledges risks following an award-winning Venice and Toronto run, a breakout Italian box office, and New Line Cinema securing English-language remake rights to Italy’s Oscar entry for Best International Film.
articles.content:
Paolo Strippoli has been making waves on the festival circuit, starting with Venice , where his psychological horror thriller The Spiral ( L’Estranea ) debuted. Now, he is leading an awards season campaign for Italy’s official Oscar entry for Best International Film.

But after Fellini, a Hollywood darling, Giuseppe Tornatore, Roberto Benigni, Paola Sorentino earlier won Oscar trophies with their movies, the Italian genre specialist is paving a new road to possible gold statues for his country with early buzz and prestigious awards. Ahead of an awards season screening of The Spiral for Academy voters in Toronto on Tuesday night, Strippoli talked to The Hollywood Reporter about what he wants to avoid and get right as he shows off his critically and commercially successful thriller. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Business "Alarming" Diversity Backtrack Happening In Film and TV Industry In Canada, Report Finds TV Why Mike Flanagan Just Couldn't Kill Carrie White

And that includes curbing aspirations. “We know we have strong contenders. So as we go on, and the competition grows, it’s risky for your well-being. So I try to lower expectations. I try to enjoy this time meeting people, showing the film in different countries,” Strippoli explained. His low expectations could, however, be a tactical advantage as the Oscar campaign for The Spiral, backed by the Italian government and industry, looks to advance by exceeding predictions for the best international film competition.

In many ways, The Spiral has come out of nowhere to earn Oscar contention. After his third feature, Holy Boy, premiered out of competition in Venice, festival artistic director Alberto Barbera blessed with a competition berth Strippoli’s fourth feature and escalating horror pic about a wife and mother taking her family to ever-darker places over a fear of an imperfect family. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In Venice, the hometown audience gave Strippoli and his cast – including Jasmine Trinca, Valeria Bruni Tedeschi, Romana Maggiora Vergano, Adriano Giannini and Andrea Genovese – a nine-minute standing ovation and strong reviews, and that was followed by the horror thriller voted the first runner-up for the People's Choice Midnight Madness Award at the Toronto Film Festival.

It didn’t take long after that for The Spiral starring Trinca as a mother drawn into a Faustian pact with a mysterious stranger played by Bruni Tedeschi to be tapped as Italy’s submission for the best international feature Oscar, and the first for a homegrown genre film. “I’m very proud because it’s my movie, but I also interpret this as a great signal for genre cinema in Italy, and we’re fighting to go further as possible to hopefully make it to the short list,” Strippoli said.

The director, who co-wrote the film's screenplay with Salvatore De Chirico, kicks off his horror movie with a generational fight between Trinca as Anna, a frantic mother confessing a lie to Alice, her estranged daughter played by Maggiora Vergano, that she insists destroyed her family — and while all dark rainstorm rages out the apartment window.

“I care about the intimate story of the characters, but what really fascinates me is how I can talk about the outside world, the whole society around these characters,” Strippoli explained of the raw emotions of the mother and daughter in the apartment corresponding to an intensifying Biblical flood outside. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Their family's downfall over 25 years unfolds in The Spiral across four chapters, centered on a Faustian bargain between Anna and The Stranger (Bruni Tedeschi). Strippoli and co-writer De Chirico deliberately crafted The Stranger not as a dark, Satanic figure, but as a mischievous entity who gracefully exploits the greed and cunning of the affluent Anna.

“It was beautiful to work with them,” Strippoli said in praise of Trinca and Bruni Tedschi. “I wanted their relationship to be carnal, sapphic. Because Anna is so stiff in everyday life, and when she is with The Stranger, for her it’s a liberating experience,” the director explained.

Theatrical audiences have responded to this tale of a desperate housewife and her graceful messenger of evil. The Venice competition launch and buzz also helped lift The Spiral to surpassing $4 million at the Italian box office since bowing on Oct. 8.

Strippoli’s film also had a Nov. 17 screening in Los Angeles for Oscar voters just as the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences after the Thanksgiving break gets set to draw up an Oscar shortlist for best international feature. Spain’s La Bola Negra is the heavy favorite, but Strippoli’s Italian backers are betting The Spiral can move up behind leaders like Romania’s Palme d’Or winner Fjord , France’s Minotaur and South Korea’s Possible Love to make the shortlist of 15 films to be announced on Dec. 15.

In the meantime, New Line Cinema has won a competitive bid for the English language remake rights to The Spiral, a deal that includes the Paramount label also getting distribution rights to the Italian film in North America and a host of international territories. New Line also plans a limited theatrical release for the Italian-language film before the end of 2026 to ensure Oscar season contention. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The Spiral filmmakers have inevitably received Hollywood horror scripts from major studios and streamers looking for the next Backrooms and Obsession after the summer breakout box office success of those thriller chillers. But as he looks to drive award season attention for his film, Strippoli said he needs balance commercial expectations with creative ambitions.

“Every time I work on something, I don’t do so with expectations. Of course I deal with expectations. But in my job, in my work, expectations can change the nature of a project for the worse,” he warns. Strippoli said trying to match creative expectations with a producer’s commercial assumptions risks ending in failure.

“I won’t succeed, and my movie will worse than it should be and could be,” he argued. For that reason, Strippoli insists on an authenticity and honesty in his work to better his chances of connecting with and speaking to audiences.

“I think people value honesty and people need be contradicted at times. They want to be surprised. They don’t want to be treated like children. They are paying for a vision and you have to give a vision, so expectations are never good,” he adds. So while Strippoli hinted at one his next movies possibly being another genre pic, and even an English language film for a more diverse cast, he's also looking beyond an Oscar race for The Spiral for his next finished script and adventure on a film set.

“I really miss the set. I really love the family you build on set. And finally seeing what you imagined coming to life and it’s beautiful,” he said.

(Image credit: NBC) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter There was no doubt that Dolly Parton tribute night at The Voice would be special. NBC’s long-running singing competition, which is currently airing on the 2026 TV schedule , brought the Top 10 together to perform duets to the greatest hits from the late country icon . It was an hour of performances that were entertaining and emotional as each pairing came from different teams, allowing the coaches to work together in rehearsals for the first time.

All of the performances had an added weight to them because the coaches and singers clearly wanted to do the legendary Dolly Parton justice. After a group performance of “9 to 5” that included an entire troupe of backing dancers, BigCountry (Team Queen) and Dakota Cohen (Team Adam) kicked things off with a rockin’ version of “Jolene” that was big on personality and a fun blend of country and rock. It was smart to start the night with such a jolt of energy, allowing the competitors to keep riding that wave all night.

When it finally came time for the most anticipated song of the night in any Dolly Parton tribute, it was up to Connor Closs (Team Adam) and Brianna Cameron (Team Kelly) to tackle “I Will Always Love You.” A song so big it’s terrifying for any singer to take on, let alone a male vocalist and a 14-year-old, these two beautifully blended their vocals in ways that allowed them to uplift each other and soar even higher. Hands down, it was a showstopper, and it stepped Brianna up as a real contender to win it all.

While it was clear the duet of “I Will Always Love You” stole the show, it definitely wasn’t the only memorable performance of the episode. Ferryn & Brinkley (Team Riley) and Kyle Davis (Team Kelly) were paired up on “Islands in the Stream.” It was already charming that the 61-year-old dad was dueting with sisters who are the age of his own daughters and they had a very father-daughter vibe going on. But the reveal that Ferryn & Brinkley both work full-time at Dollywood, the amusement park owned by Dolly Parton herself, and that they even had footage of Ferryn on stage with the icon was really special to see.

Since first appearing at the Blind Auditions, Ferryn & Brinkley have been hugely marketable. From their talent to their personalities, they look and feel like they could easily join the ranks of country stars who've also broken big in movies and TV , whether they ultimately win The Voice or not. As we move ever closer to the unveiling of the winning coach and star , it’s getting harder and harder to watch the singers get sent home, but I get the feeling that many of them are going to have a life in entertainment beyond this season.

Seeing Dolly Parton in past The Voice appearances being her sassy self really helped make up for some of that and was a fitting way to remember her.

articles.title: NBC Tracking Storm Due To Hit 100th Annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade: Will Balloons Be Grounded?
articles.summary: NBC is closely tracking a Thanksgiving storm expected to bring high winds and heavy rain to New York City and much of the Eastern U.S. The network's coverage of the 100th edition of the annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade will air on NBC and stream on Peacock from 8:30 a.m. to noon ET. The parade […]
articles.content:
NBC is keeping close watch on a Thanksgiving storm expected to bring high winds and heavy rain to New York City and much of the Eastern U.S.

The network's coverage of the 100th edition of the annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade will air on NBC and stream on Peacock from 8:30 a.m. to noon ET. The parade remains a significant draw, with last year's pulling in 34.3 million viewers across NBC and Peacock, its biggest combined audience on record .

Tyler Roys, a senior meteorologist with AccuWeather, said in an interview with Deadline that the second half of the parade seems to be at the most risk of being disrupted. He said the winds will be "near criteria" for grounding balloons – a signature feature of the New York City event, along with marching bands and floats. "They have some decisions to make over the next 48 hours," Roys added. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

NBC's affiliate in New York expects it to be "a close call" if conditions on the Midtown Manhattan streets fall below city rules mandating that balloons be grounded in sustained winds of 24 miles per hour or gusts higher than 35 mph.

The Nor'easter, a classic storm pattern, is expected to take shape. By Thursday morning, sustained winds are expected to be 12-25 miles an hour with gusts of 20 to 30 mph, increasing over the course of the day.

In honor of NBC's broadcasting centennial, the parade is set to have 100 large balloons. The "All-Star Broadway Thanksgiving Day Celebration" will feature numerous shows in a 10-minute medley. The balloons have only been grounded once before, in 1971.

About 3 million people watch the parade live, with the Manhattan skyscrapers creating a wind tunnel that can heighten the effects of the weather . "Our team is closely monitoring the weather forecast with our city and agency partners, and as always, the safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority," NBC said in a statement provided to Deadline. "Decisions regarding balloon flight will be made on parade morning based on weather conditions and established safety protocols."

NBCUniversal's ad sales teams have been pushing the 100th anniversary, and the division said Monday it had established a revenue record for the parade. "Do you keep up with the news?" the billionaire asks the UK's most prestigious architect via video call. "So you're talking about some kind of revolution?" Miguel Moreno replies.

"Uh, full-scale collapse of the system we live," he's told.

That's the setup for Bunker , Florian Zeller 's thriller starring Javier Bardem and Penélope Cruz that wowed the Venice Film Festival. Check out the trailer above.

Here's the logline: When an architect (Bardem) accepts a morally ambiguous project — building a survivalist bunker for a tech billionaire (Paul Dano) — his wife (Cruz) begins to question their marriage after 17 years together. The dramatic thriller examines the emotional and moral challenges faced by a couple as the anxieties of an increasingly uncertain world begin to reshape their marriage, exploring the fears, doubts and ethical dilemmas that define our time. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });
