Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google When someone mentions the name Supergirl , the person who springs to everyone's mind is Kara Zor-El. AS one of the few surviving Kryptonians and Superman's cousin, Kara has proven time and again that she's one of the greatest heroes in all of DC, even though she rarely gets the credit or spotlight she deserves. As with any iconic role, plenty of other characters have taken up the Supergirl mantle when Kara was unavailable. The most famous of these are Matrix and Linda Danvers, both filling the role before Kara made her post- Crisis debut, and the most recent example is Thundergirl , who actually is filling in as the Maid of Might in the ongoing Supergirl (2025) series.

However, as iconic as Kara is, she actually wasn't the first heroine to rock the S-shield. She might be the original Supergirl, but months before she literally rocketed into Superman's world, a very different gal called herself Super-Girl, complete with Kara's looks, powers, and costume, to boot. Of course, she only appeared for one issue, and it's clear that this version served as a testing ground for the conceit of the character, but therein lies a lost art of comic book character introductions. Super-Girl is one of the most pivotal characters in DC, and she's the embodiment of this forgotten style of superheroic introductions.

This version of Super-Girl made her singular appearance in Superman (1939) #123. Jimmy Olsen, as he is wont to do, came into possession of a wish-granting staff, and his first thought was to create a female companion who could fight alongside Superman to keep him safe and give him companionship. Super-Girl fit the bill perfectly, proving she had all of Superman's many marvelous powers. However, she lacked the experience he did, so she wound up getting in his way more often than she did help him. She even nearly revealed his identity to Lois after X-raying through his outer outfit. In the end, however, she wound up saving the Man of Steel, sacrificing herself to save Superman from a Kryptonite attack. As she succumbed to Kryptonite poisoning, she asked that Jimmy undo his wish, making her cease to exist.

It's a morbid end to this introduction, but it did what it had to do, as it posed the question of whether fans would want a Supergirl in the first place. By creating a character made to expire by the end of the issue, the creators were able to gauge fans' reactions to Super-Girl as a concept. If they hated her, they could sweep this under the rug as a one-off adventure. But since they loved Super-Girl, they were incentivized to create the proper version just nine months later. Obviously, introducing a character like Kara wasn't something they could walk back from, and the heads at DC were likely very nervous about the whole thing, so using Super-Girl as a test was a perfect middle ground. On top of that, she serves as the perfect example of how characters used to be introduced .

Super-Girl's origin is definitely strange, but back in the day, the idea of introducing a superhero in the main issue of another character's ongoing was the premier way of debuting. Often, these heroes would join in on a story and then race off to their own back issues or side adventures in an anthology book, before eventually claiming their own place in an ongoing, if they proved popular enough. Supergirl would take that path, but she more often served as a main and side character in Superman's adventures as well, with other characters like the Elongated Man also fitting this role.

Nowadays, however, breakout heroes don't tend to be introduced in this same way. Instead, more often than not, they debut in team books. Don't get me wrong, plenty of new heroes grace heroes' main book pages every month, but they aren't typically designed as breakout stars. Jade Tiger swung onto the pages of Batgirl (2025) and Marilyn Moonlight in Superman (2023), but these characters more serve as supporting cast members rather than heroes designed to lead their own adventures. Meanwhile, team books like Teen Titans (2026) and New Titans (2026) introduce entire casts of new characters, from the bionic Eva to the bad-luck-inducing Wildcard.

It makes sense to throw a new hero designed to break away onto a team, as it gives them a reason to stay in the public eye for a longer time as they battle alongside established heroes instead of relying on one or two issues for them to build an audience. New characters still do show up in solo books, but it's much rarer, as it takes a much bigger chance that the character will make a scant few appearances before being relegated to event-only limbo, or even worse, back-up feature-only jail. Still, DC testing the waters with more heroes debuting in solo adventures could be something to explore once again, as it keeps the focus squarely on one or two heroes instead of an entire team, which can easily be spread too thin.

What's your preferred method of introducing new characters? Let us know in the comments below!

South Park Season 29 kicked off its run earlier this year with some big changes to the formula. Not only did it change the name of the show and town to "South America," but it also returned to form by killing off Kenny at the end of the premiere episode . But it seems like the series is going back on it now.

South Park Season 29 has now reached the end of its confirmed six episodes previously scheduled with Comedy Central with the final of these episodes making their debut on Wednesday, November 25th. It seems like the animated series is going all out for the occasion, and with the final episode now slated, Comedy Central has dropped the first look at what's coming and you can check it out in action below.

South Park Season 29 Episode 6 is titled "City Endings" and will be making its debut with Comedy Central on Wednesday, November 25th at 10PM ET/PT before being available to stream exclusively with Paramount+ the next day in the United States, Canada and Australia. While the rest of the season had been hinging on some sort of reveal for Grand Theft Auto VI or the midterm elections , that doesn't seem to be the case for this episode as it's going to reference some more recent current events.

The synopsis for the episode teases it as such, "When mysterious power outages strike South America, the townspeople fear Chinese cyberattacks. It’s up to the boys to discover what’s really going on." But with the previous episode seemingly moving away from the midterm election results (and likely Grand Theft Auto ) , it seems like creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone have figured out a new path forward. And that seems to involve Kenny in some way with the special preview image you can find below.

South Park killed off Kenny at the start of the season, and even saw him replaced by a new little version of Randy for one of the episodes . But it seems like the finale is going to reset everything once more as this "City Ending" for the season will find a way to wrap up all of the stories that had been ongoing in a seemingly unsatisfying fashion. But that just seems like the joke at play, so we'll have to see how it actually all works out as the season comes to an end.

There's still a question amidst all of this, however, as South Park Studios' deal with Paramount meant that Parker and Stone need to deliver at least ten episodes of the series a year over the course of five years. With this season seemingly capping off with six episodes, there could be an announcement for future scheduled episodes to come after this one airs. Or maybe a slate of new specials for the holidays.

What are you hoping to see in South Park Season 29's potential finale? How have you liked the season so overall? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.summary: This is less-than-positive news for the long-running show.
articles.content:
CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss has made headlines for multiple reasons since being hired for the job in October 2025, but one specific aspect of the job she continues to receive backlash for is 60 Minutes . This past summer, Weiss and executive producer Nick Bilton cut ties with several high-profile employees and, more recently, the show has seen losses in viewership. Now, some fresh numbers regarding the news magazine show’s 59th season have arrived, and they mark yet another setback for Weiss and her staff.

Months ago, Season 59 premiered to 6.5 million viewers on CBS, and that sum differed from the initial report of 7.7 million (which was not finalized at the time). One of the key commonalities between both reports, however, is that the news program has seen losses within the 25-54 demographic. In that demo, 60 has apparently seen a 25 percent decline compared to last season. This demographic is critical, especially when considering on-air advertising.

After parting ways with Pelley and co., Weiss hired several other broadcasters to fill out 60 Minutes ’ new broadcasting team. Ross Douthat, Gianna Toboni, Sebastian Junger, Sir Trevor Phillips and Ariel Levy were ultimately brought on. Those newcomers are now working alongside the show’s three on-camera veterans: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker and Jon Wertheim. Just recently, Stahl addressed the backlash she faced due to remaining with the show under Weiss’ leadership and said she did so in order for the series as they know it not to “vanish.”

articles.title: ‘Naughty’ vs ‘Nasty’: Universal and Warner Bros. Battle Over Titles for New Jennifer Aniston, Jenna Ortega Movies (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Two similarly titled movies are causing a war of words between Universal and Warner Bros. Pictures. The legacy studios are locked in a stalemate over dueling projects that sound alike and are set to hit theaters around the same time, five sources tell Variety. The first is “Naughty,” Olivia Wilde’s raucous Christmas comedy starring Jennifer […]
articles.content:
Two similarly titled movies are causing a war of words between Universal and Warner Bros . Pictures. The legacy studios are locked in a stalemate over dueling projects that sound alike and are set to hit theaters around the same time, five sources tell Variety .

The first is “ Naughty ,” Olivia Wilde’s raucous Christmas comedy starring Jennifer Aniston. The other is “ Nasty ,” Mary Bronstein’s psychological drama led by Jenna Ortega, which will roll out under Warner’s new indie label Clockwork. Universal slated “Naughty” for Nov. 5, 2027, after registering the name with the Motion Picture Association in 2023, according to two sources. Clockwork, the nascent shingle run by Neon veteran Christian Parkes, has not officially set a date for “Nasty,” though four sources say the film is also eyeing a November 2027 release. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories ‘PAW Patrol’ Spinoff Series ‘Skye’s Pup Squad’ Set for 2027 Release

Generally, studios go to great lengths to avoid delivering movies with similar-sounding names — much less launching them in the same corridor. “Naughty” and “Nasty” aren’t alike in genre or subject matter. “Naughty,” featuring Aniston and Peter Dinklage, follows a single mom who has to convince Santa Claus to testify at her divorce hearing. “Nasty,” Bronstein’s follow-up to “If I Had Legs I’d Kick You,” revolves around an elite gymnast competing for a spot on the Olympic team while dealing with her manipulative coach.

Yet insiders at Universal and Warner Bros. feel the fact that the titles are basically synonyms could confuse moviegoers. Further complicating the matter is that LuckyChap, Margot Robbie’s prolific film and TV production shop, is backing both projects. Universal and Clockwork declined to comment. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The spat is headed toward a formal review by the MPA, which has a 101-year-old department called the Title Registration Bureau to manage such conflicts. Arbitration involves a panel of studio intellectual property lawyers at the ready to hash it out. Although titles are not copyrightable, the TRB is armed with a 50-page document outlining rules of play and precedent, per one source, and its rulings are legally binding. The MPA declined to comment on the matter.

"Movies want to distinguish themselves, and the first way they do that is the title," says Jeff Bock, an analyst with Exhibitor Relations. "If they sound similar, there could be confusion."

Universal believes it should have dibs since it was first to file with “Naughty.” That would mean “Nasty” either changes its name or shifts its release date. Insiders note Clockwork filed two alternative titles for “Nasty” with its MPA documentation, but the filmmakers are against using the backups.

Meanwhile, sources close to “Nasty” feel that Universal is “punching down” at Clockwork because the indie drama doesn’t have the same broad commercial appeal as the Aniston-led holiday comedy. (Though Clockwork is a specialty label, it is owned and operated by the vast Skydance Motion Picture Group). Wilde is content to let “Nasty” proceed as titled, according to a person familiar with her thinking. LuckyChap is working toward a solution that sets up both projects for success without entering MPA arbitration, two sources add.

Disputes like these rarely become public knowledge, insiders say. And most often, studios work it out without involving the Title Registration Bureau. The group’s last two arbitrations were in 2018. That’s when Disney and Lucasfilm settled on “Solo: A Star Wars Story” rather than “Solo” to distinguish the Han Solo origin story from the 2018 climbing documentary “Free Solo.” And Universal agreed to change its raunchy comedy to “Blockers” from “The Pact,” a name that was already used by a 2012 horror film.

Renaming movies can benefit both parties. Ask Paramount and Sony, which released “No Strings Attached” and “Friends With Benefits” a few months apart in 2011. Both romantic comedies — one starring Natalie Portman and Ashton Kutcher and the other with Mila Kunis and Justin Timberlake — had an identical premise involving two friends who agree to casual sex without dating. “No Strings Attached” was originally called “Friends With Benefits,” but the studio acquiesced to the title change. Any plot similarities didn't dilute the films’ respective box office, with each one grossing $149 million globally. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

To that end, movies with similar themes or ideas are less of a problem for studios. Bock points to 1998’s “Armageddon” and “Deep Impact,” two disaster films about comets on a collision course with Earth. Both were theatrical winners, with “Armageddon” earning $553 million globally and “Deep Impact” generating $350 million globally.

“Consumers might be fooled by something like that, but it didn’t affect the box office," he says. "They turned out to be different, even though the synopsis was the same."

articles.title: Montel Williams Gets Candid About the State of Daytime TV: "The Talk Shows of My Era Became the Reality Shows of Today"
articles.summary: The former 'Montel Williams Show' host talks about how short attention spans have changed the daytime talk show landscape during a conversation on the 'We're Out of Time' podcast with host Richard Taite.
articles.content:
Montel Williams is getting candid about the state of daytime talk show, saying viewers' attention spans have changed a lot since he ended his own talker in 2008.

"It's a sad commentary that we lost our attention span in the last 15 years," he said in a conversation with We’re Out of Time podcast host Richard Taite, debuting Tuesday. "The talk shows that I did and the talk shows of that era were hourlong talk discussions. We don't have the patience anymore to listen to a topic for an hour. I say the majority of people don't." Related Stories TV 'Property Brother' Jonathan Scott Is Getting a Daytime Talk Show TV Montel Williams Hospitalized After Workout, Spokesman Says

He said the format has morphed quite a bit since his show ended. ( The Montel Williams Show ran from July 1991 to May 2008, spanning 17 seasons.) blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"So the talk shows of my era became the reality shows of today," he opined. "I'll say that again, the talk shows of my era became the reality shows of today. We took the dysfunction that we put on display and turned those into individual shows of their own, to the point now that the talk that's out there right now, what do they really even talk? Other than selling products and hawking a new movie or hawking a new record, what do they do? Is there any discussion that makes man better?"

Williams was quick to say he's not criticizing anyone in particular, just nothing how times have changed.

"I'm not casting aspersion on my peers of the day," he said. "But I am saying that at least back when we talked about issues, we talked about issues that changed the world, that I believe changed America. We were talking about AIDS before any news stations were going full reports on it. We were talking about civil unrest, we were talking about racism, we were talking about hate, we were talking about all those things that we didn't even talk about it around the dinner table. We talked about it. Some of us did it in the salacious way. But at least they had a discussion." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Williams added that the goal with his show was to educate people and put a spotlight on a topic that viewers perhaps hadn't been introduced to or thought that much about. In other words, something that would "make you stop and think," he said.

Does he think that kind of talk show would work today?

"It could, if it was formatted differently," he says. "I think we can go an entire hour, but we have to go in that hour introducing every single piece of that topic, not just one piece, but we have to introduce it all and add to it information that people can take away."

Taite likened that to scrolling on your phone, where you're staying engaged by absorbing different information — and a lot of it — in a short time span.

"That's right, and [keeping] you stimulated on the same topic instead of scrolling, or swiping up and down, instead of doing that and getting a different topic every single second, and that's what they're trying to do," Williams replied. "They're trying to give you something different every five or six minutes where they never really even solved the first five minutes. I say that every single topic out there can be broken into 20 different topics. Somebody needs to just program it that way."

He added, “I think we may gravitate back to that as soon as we realize that we pushed attention span to a point where it's no longer attention span.”

Given that the studio has never been shy about embracing the weird side , this inclusion isn't surprising and fits right into that tradition. With this mission, players can follow Jason and Lucia into the depths of Hell and battle the Devil and his army of demons. This may take the cake as far as supernatural encounters go, in both Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption .

Many of the series best discoveries come from ridiculous encounters like this , and Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't disappoint. This latest discovery in GTA 6 takes things considerably further and fits right in with the infamous Mount Chiliad mystery in Grand Theft Auto 5 and the unsettling secrets scattered throughout Red Dead Redemption 2 . But the best part of battling the Devil in this GTA 6 secret is the reward: exclusive cosmetics, a powerful shotgun, and a permanent character upgrade that makes the mission worth seeking out. But the question remains: how do you get to Hell and fight Satan in GTA 6 ?

Players looking to fight the Devil in Grand Theft Auto 6 will need to head to Port Gellhorn in Kelly County. The secret mission is accessible during Chapter 2, and players can complete it as either Jason or Lucia. However, there are some specific conditions players must meet before they can descend into Hell. Simply visiting the location during the middle of the day won't follow the recommended method for triggering the encounter. Instead, you must follow a set of guidelines shared below.

Following this sequence transports your character to Hell, where you fight an army of demons. You'll find yourself equipped with a special shotgun that makes dealing with these demonic forces easier, and eventually you'll come face-to-face with the Devil. Satan is a tough foe and will summon demons as backup, so be sure to eliminate these when they appear. Be sure to collect the Hellspawn Comshot 12 shotgun beside Satan's throne before leaving Hell.

After defeating Satan, players will awaken back at the campsite. Completing this hidden GTA 6 mission offers the Circles of Hell clothing top, a new tattoo design, the aforementioned shotgun, and a permanent health increase. The cosmetics are great, but the weapon and upgrade are the best rewards and make this mission a must-play.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is full of Easter eggs and secrets like this, and players will likely be uncovering them for years. For now, the Devil stands out as one of the more unique missions in Vice City.

The story centers the pair, two senior editors competing to oust the other from a condensed role due to impending layoffs, chasing big book deals for the publishing […]
articles.content:
Clashing Through the Snow director Carlson Young found it easy to relate to the film’s two main characters, Ryan Mitchell ( Christopher Briney ) and Hannah Hendricks ( Michelle Randolph ).

The story centers the pair, two senior editors competing to oust the other from a condensed role due to impending layoffs, chasing big book deals for the publishing company where they work. Ryan operates off of commercial motivation and tapping into what is popular to sell books while Hannah identifies as more of a literary purist who takes big swings with the depth of books she takes on.

“[The script] really spoke to me. I felt so connected to Hannah and Ryan's literary perspectives, and it felt like a existential conversation that I have with myself, moment to moment, constantly,” Young told Deadline. “It was easy for me to access their personalities and their inner worlds. And then I just loved the classic, holiday hijinks that ensue from there, and I was up for the challenge of trying to make a great holiday rom-com.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

The director connected the differing stances on what sells to challenges she navigates in her own job “balancing art and commerce, and what is and isn't viable in storytelling and in the marketplace."

“It is true that publishing and cinemas, these are tectonically shifting industries, and trying to find yourself your voice either as a book editor or director, whatever you're doing, it doesn't even need to be in a creative field,” she added. “But we're all existing in these shifting sands, and so that was my way in. That's why I was looking at it like that.”

In the below interview, Young unpacks specific moments like Lukas Gage’s “scene stealer” appearance, the Buc-ee’s knockoff Luc-ee's, Ryan’s seeking advice by talking to ChatGPT and more.

DEADLINE: I spoke with Chris and Michelle earlier, and they mentioned you gave Chris a note comparing him to Jim Carrey. Did you have any other references? Could you expand on that? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

CARLSON YOUNG: When we were rehearsing, I kept looking at him and seeing this physical comedy coming to the surface, and I was like, "This is like some Jim Carrey. I love this for you. Go off on that." We tweaked it and trimmed it and shaped it in the edit, but he's really funny. I hope that he does a lot more comedy.

DEADLINE: What was your role in the Luc-ee’s knockoff to Buc-ee’s?

YOUNG: I don't know what I can and can't say about Buc-ee’s/ Luc-ee's, but we did our best. We did our version. I'm from Texas, Buc-ee's is a big part of the psychology of a Texan, and so it was really funny, and we did our own version of it.

DEADLINE: For the part where Hannah's in the helicopter venting to the pilot and Ryan's driving the truck talking to AI, was there ever a plan to have him talking to a person or was it always going to be ChatGPT?

YOUNG: I have to say, yes, there was [a different iteration]. I personally thought that him talking to Chat was so Ryan. It made me laugh so much. And the amount of times that I've caught my husband… I'm like, ‘Are you asking ChatGPT a question? Like for real? Are you serious? ‘And he is serious. It just felt really modern and so of the times, and something like his character would actually do. And I like a lot the responses that Chat has for him. It just made me laugh.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The inclusion of many characters from the Fox era of X-Men movies is one of the most interesting aspects of Avengers: Doomsday , but the real treat is getting to see a fresh attempt at getting Cyclops right. While those Fox X-Men films did a lot of things right and fans still fondly remember them, most people agree that th e handling of Scott Summers, aka Cyclops, was a problem . Despite having a notable actor in James Marsden in the role, the movies didn't prioritize the character, which was hugely disappointing to fans who fell in love with Cyclops on the pages of the comic book and in X-Men: The Animated Series .

Thankfully, James Marsden is back as Cyclops in Avengers: Doomsday and has announced that we will finally see his version of the character done right. Rather than being used purely as a pawn in a love triangle with Wolverine and Jean Grey , this big-screen take on Cyclops will showcase him as what he truly is at heart, which is a leader. It's exactly what many of us have wanted from Scott Summers in a movie, especially after seeing the character handled so well recently in the X-Men '97 animated series.

While promoting the epic blockbuster Avengers: Doomsday , James Marsden spoke with Sharp Magazine . They talked about what made him return to the role, especially since many would agree that the character was handled so poorly in the past. He talked with Marvel Studios and the Russo Brothers, who wanted to take an authentic approach to Cyclops, which includes showing him as a leader. Marsden didn't want this return to just be a small cameo, which he had already done at the end of X-Men: Days of Future Past .

"One of the things people have said for years is that Cyclops is a leader, yet in many of the previous films he often took a back seat to Wolverine and some of the other characters," Marsden said. "There are only so many minutes available in a film this large, but it was important to me that my return felt meaningful." The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday just released and seems to cement the idea that Cyclops will play a major role. He is shown fighting with Sam Wilson before delivering the iconic " To me, my X-Men " line as various heroes drop in alongside him.

Getting Cyclops right is important to fix the way he was done in the past, but it's also crucial to set up the future of the MCU. We already know that Kit Connor has been cast as Scott Summers in the upcoming X-Men film in 2028. If Avengers: Doomsday can give us a great Cyclops, it'll set up Scott as a true leader for the future . James Marsden certainly seems happy with what's to come in Avengers: Doomsday , adding, "I didn’t want Cyclops to simply appear for a nostalgic cameo and then disappear. I wanted there to be a genuine purpose behind his presence. Without giving anything away, I feel very good about what we were able to do with the character."

Avengers: Doomsday has to get several major things right, from establishing Doctor Doom to balancing so many characters to likely setting the table for Avengers: Secret Wars . Giving us a proper Cyclops on the big screen ranks right alongside those as it can impact the past of the X-Men and its future.

Are you excited to see Cyclops back? Let us known your thoughts on his return in the comments!

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War ended its official anime run earlier this Fall to cap over 22 years of the anime franchise. This adapted the final […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There's still one final Bleach arc that's left to tell its story, and fans deserve to see it come to fruition one day to continue from Tite Kubo's original series. Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War ended its official anime run earlier this Fall to cap over 22 years of the anime franchise . This adapted the final arc of Kubo's original manga, but that's also far from the end of the story as it is. Because back in 2021, Kubo actually continued from that finale to start something new.

When Bleach was celebrating its 20th anniversary, that's where it was first announced that the anime would be returning for a proper adaptation of Kubo's final arc. But that wasn't all as Kubo himself also came back to the pages of Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump with a new one-shot picking up from the original end of the story. Featuring an older Ichigo Kurosaki, introducing new characters, enemies and more, Bleach' s Hell Arc really needs to be fleshed out with a full sequel.

Bleach "No Breathes From Hell" was a 75 page one-shot manga release that first launched in 2021, and picks up a few years after the original end of the series. Exploring more of the ten year time skip seen with the original finale, Kazui and Ichika have grown a bit older and more of the Soul Society rankings have filled out with the new one-shot introducing some new members to each squad. Kazui has grown much stronger, and the Soul Society is preparing for a special bit of funeral rites for the late Ukitake. But things get more complicated from there.

A massive skeletal being arrives with no one other than Ichika being able to sense it before it makes its move, and it's revealed that these new monsters don't have any spiritual pressure of their own. Soon enough, the formerly defeated Szayelaporro arrives and reveals that he was cast into Hell after his defeat. It's a brand new region that has never been referenced before, and with it has granted him an entirely new level of dark power that seems to have given him godly new abilities.

Soul Society begins to get covered in a dark matter known as "Phosphoplasm" and an entire new class of beings is revealed. Beings with too strong spiritual pressure never return completely to the Soul Society and are said to have been sent somewhere else and thus cast into Hell. This includes former enemies and even former Soul Reapers that have died in battle. With the final pages of the one shot, Bleach kicks off the "New Breathes From Hell" arc with no signs of continuing after five long years.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War' s anime finale has now put a final button on the story, but this one-shot remains a continuation that has yet to be touched even after five years of inactivity. This new sequel teases returns from not only some of those most memorable villains of the past, but also new and terrifying versions of each of the major fan favorite Soul Reapers that have died along the way. There's even a potential to see some of the Soul Reapers that had never been even shown until they were teased in the anime like the first generation of fighters .

But after spending all this time to bring back Bleach through the anime, and even having Kubo continue the franchise's story with a new one-shot and even the Burn the Witch spinoff series, there's clearly an interest from the creator to keep messing around with the story . A new sequel would be the perfect way to keep it going, but there are also other potential issues that spring up as a result. That includes the potential schedule for which Kubo would need to abide by. That probably seems like the biggest hurdle to overcome, but not an impossible one.

Shueisha's editorial department has worked with their notable creators before to work out a schedule that's for the creators' benefit like seen with Hunter x Hunter' s Yoshihiro Togashi. They've already done that with Kubo's work on Burn the Witch, so it's possible that they could work out a new schedule that could allow this sequel to exist. Where it's a big chapter coming out every few months, weekly, or even once a year, Bleach just needs to continue so we can see what's next . Would you want to see more of Bleach' s Hell Arc? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: Francis Lawrence Signed On for One 'Hunger Games' Movie. Five Films Later, He's the Keeper of Panem
articles.summary: The 'Sunrise on the Reaping' director looks back on the pressure of taking over a franchise, his decade-long collaboration with Suzanne Collins, why the series endures, and where things stand on ‘Constantine 2’ and 'Red Rising.'
articles.content:
The morning after the New York premiere of The Hunger Games : Sunrise on the Reaping , Francis Lawrence is still taking in the view from the night before.

On one red carpet stood nearly every era of Panem. There were the newcomers: Joseph Zada , Whitney Peak and Mckenna Grace, along with franchise first-timers Kieran Culkin, Elle Fanning, Jesse Plemons, Ralph Fiennes and Glenn Close. Tom Blyth, Rachel Zegler and Josh Andrés Rivera who starred in Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes prequel, were in attendance. And there were the originals, Jennifer Lawrence , Josh Hutcherson , Woody Harrelson , Elizabeth Banks, Jena Malone and Willow Shields assembled like the franchise's own Avengers. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies New 'Hunger Games' Movie on the Way? Lionsgate Film Chief Shares Latest on Franchise's Future Beyond the Book 'Percy Jackson and the Olympians': How Season 3 Brings Epic Moments to Life and Deals With Annabeth's Absence in the Books

"Last night at the premiere, for the first time, we had three generations of cast," Lawrence tells The Hollywood Reporter of the Nov. 16 event. "There's something really special about the time we've all spent together and the quality of people I've gotten to work with."

Lawrence has been a constant across all of them. Since taking over from director Gary Ross with 2013's Catching Fire , he has directed every Hunger Games film that followed, working alongside producer Nina Jacobson to turn Suzanne Collins' dystopian saga following teenagers forced into fatal combat into one of Hollywood's most dependable franchises. The original four films grossed roughly $2.98 billion worldwide, and Collins' five books have sold more than 100 million copies globally, growing into one of the most successful young adult publishing franchises in history.

Still, the scale didn't fully hit him until the final Mockingjay films. Around the release of the films, The Hunger Games: The Exhibition opened to fans, and Lawrence walked through it with his stars. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Walking through it for the first time with Jen and Josh, and I think Liam [Hemsworth] was there, we were all just stunned that we had made something museum-worthy, with our music, our costumes, our props, pieces of our sets and the lore," he recalls. "There's something really special in that, knowing these stories have connected with people in a certain way."

Amid the success, it's easy to forget that Lawrence arrived in Panem as an outsider. He had never made a sequel to someone else's first film, and on Catching Fire he was "joining an existing family," with a cast "so big and so seasoned" that he felt he had a lot to prove. He also assumed it would be a one-time job.

"The weird thing is, when I signed on to Catching Fire , I thought that was going to be the only one I did," he says.

Instead, the studio asked him to stay for the two-part Mockingjay . "A huge part of me is very appreciative of being invited to keep making these movies and be part of this team."

That invitation, however, came with a nerve-racking stretch. A few weeks into shooting Mockingjay , production paused for a month so Lawrence and the team could promote and release Catching Fire . He would face its box office verdict with most of the next film's shoot still ahead of him.

"Man, what if this thing bombs?" he remembers thinking of the pressure for Catching Fire success amid filming the third installment. "I now still have like 125 days of shooting with all of these people that are going to be looking at me like, 'We just made a movie with this guy that bombed.'" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

He needn't have worried. After its 2013 release, Catching Fire became the franchise's highest grossing film, and the once outsider became the keeper of the series. "The series was quite popular at that point, and there was a lot of excitement and confidence at the studio, so that was nice," he says.

When Lawrence and Jacobson returned eight years later with 2023's The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes , the odds felt less certain. The prequel had no Katniss and centered on the rise of the tyrant Coriolanus Snow, played by Donald Sutherland in the original films with Tom Blyth taking on the role for a younger version.

"A bunch of time had gone by, and you wonder if there's still an appetite for Hunger Games , especially Hunger Games without Katniss," he says. "It had a very different structure, and it was a story about the person everybody hates, so a lot of things made me a little nervous."

Sunrise on the Reaping , which traces the origins of the fan-favorite mentor Haymitch Abernathy, felt different.

"Weirdly, this one I kind of felt less pressure," Lawrence says. "I felt much more confident that this was one that fans really wanted to see, and it felt like a return to form for movies like Catching Fire and the original."

There being a new Hunger Games book came as a surprise to Lawrence, who assures he, along with Jacobson, are just as in the dark as everyone else. After more than a decade of working together, Lawrence and Collins have a routine. She keeps quiet while she writes, and only once her publisher confirms she has a book does she bring in Lawrence and Jacobson, always with the same modest question of whether the story is a movie. Lawrence and Jacobson always say yes. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

For Sunrise , Lawrence and Jacobson got word of the novel earlier than ever, and the secrecy was tighter as a result. The manuscript was kept at Collins‘ agent's home, and then then moved to a locked safe kept with Jacobson. Screenwriter Billy Ray wrote on an offline laptop in Jacobson's office, while Lawrence stayed busy making secret trips to read it.

"This one we got further in advance, while she was still going back and forth with her editors," he says. "I had read it a couple of times, Nina had read it a couple of times, and I went to New York to work with Suzanne on breaking down the book into what we thought the movie would be. We hired [original screenwriter] Billy Ray. He was already writing and we were having calls about the draft. So a lot of work was done before the book was even announced, and I couldn't talk to anybody about it."

The book and its film adaptation were announced together in June 2024, which brought "a lot of relief,” he says. "At least then people knew we were working on it and that it was the Haymitch story. We just had to keep quiet about the storyline itself.”

That left the biggest challenge: finding a young Haymitch, the carefree kid from District 12 long before he became the drunken, broken mentor Harrelson made iconic. The search led to Zada, the breakout from Prime Video's We Were Liars and Netflix's East of Eden . Lawrence put him "through the wringer" in auditions before landing on the actor to carry the beloved character's origin story. articles.title: I Don't Think Enough People Talk About What A Masterpiece From The '90s 12 Monkeys Is
articles.summary: Pulp Fiction is great and all, but what about 12 Monkeys?!
articles.content:
When discussing movies from the ‘90s, there are some films that get mentioned all the time. I'm talking about movies like Pulp Fiction , The Silence of the Lambs , and, of course, The Shawshank Redemption (Even though I think it's just “good” and not great).

However, do you want to know what movie ISN’T on our list? The 1995 masterpiece (Yes, masterpiece) 12 Monkeys . I actually think it’s one of the best films from that decade, and here’s why.

A lot of people like to bring up great opening scenes in films , but do you know what I don’t think gets enough credit? Great opening songs, and look, I get it. Many older, typically black-and-white films (or westerns!) began with opening credits and stirring music before we met the characters. But nowadays, most films jump right into the action (in medias res, as it were).

I love a good time travel story , and 12 Monkeys has one of my favorites of any film. The story concerns a convict named Cole (Bruce Willis) who is sent back in time to investigate what caused the virus that killed 99% of the human population. He’s tasked with learning who the “Army of the 12 Monkeys” are, since they’re suspected of releasing the virus, as there are records of them writing, “We did it!”

Lastly, Brad Pitt is just so good in this movie. He plays a mental asylum patient, and the closest thing I can compare his performance to is Johnny Depp wigging out in Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas .

EXCLUSIVE: Theatrical tech, distribution and management corp Qube Cinema has hired Imax and 20th Century Fox distribution vet Craig Dehmel as their new Head of Studio Relations.

Dehmel will be based in Los Angeles for Qube Wire, which has a global content distribution service which connects with over 7,000 theaters worldwide. In his new position, Dehmel will lead strategic customer development and strengthen senior-level relationships across Hollywood studios, independent distributors, and content owners.

Dehmel's 35 years in the motion picture industry includes serving as Head of Global Distribution at Imax, where he led the planning, programming, and distribution of Hollywood studio, local-language, documentary, and special-content releases across more than 1,700 Imax screens worldwide.
